EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows clear signatures of an aliphatic nitro-containing amide. 1) Two NO₂–related bands appear at 1487 cm⁻¹ and 1277 cm⁻¹, matching the typical νas(NO₂) / νs(NO₂) pair (rule GFQ-022). 2) A strong band at 861 cm⁻¹ is consistent with NO₂ out-of-plane bending / N–O wag. 3) The intense carbonyl stretch at 1694 cm⁻¹ fits an amide / carbamate C=O. 4) N–H stretching features are present at 3318–3212 cm⁻¹, required by an NH group; no OH stretch is required (3418 cm⁻¹ is weak). 5) Additional bands at 1131 and 1083 cm⁻¹ correspond to C–O/C–N stretches expected in a carbamate. Among the candidates only molecule 6 (CC(C)OC(=O)N[N+](=O)[O-]) contains an amide carbonyl, an NH, a nitro group and an alkoxy group, matching all these spectral elements, whereas the other candidates lack either NO₂ or the necessary functional combination.
